name: J₁–J₂ · 10 × 10
geometry: 10 by 10 square lattice; periodic in both directions; each nearest-neighbor and diagonal next-nearest-neighbor bond counted once
hamiltonian: H = J1 sum_<ij> S_i · S_j + J2 sum_<<ij>> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J1 = 1; J2 = 0.5; no constant shift

name: Triangular Heisenberg · 12 × 12
geometry: 12 by 12 triangular Bravais lattice; periodic along both primitive vectors; nearest-neighbor displacements (1,0), (0,1), (1,-1), each undirected bond counted once
hamiltonian: H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift

name: Hubbard · 8 × 8
geometry: 8 by 8 square lattice; periodic in both directions; nearest-neighbor hopping only
hamiltonian: H = -t sum_<ij>,s (c†_is c_js + h.c.) + U sum_i n_iup n_idown; t = 1; U = 8; tprime = 0; no chemical-potential term or constant shift
sector: Nup = 28; Ndown = 28; 56 electrons; ground-state variational calculation
description: Repulsive Hubbard model at U/t = 8 and one-eighth hole doping.
